questions.question_text: In the WHO World Mental Health Survey Initiative across 21 countries, which childhood adversity was reported as the most common?
questions.explanation: Parental death is the most common childhood adversity (11.0–14.8%). Physical abuse (5.3–10.8%), family violence (4.2–7.8%), and parental mental illness (5.3–6.7%) all have lower prevalence rates. Sexual abuse is not listed with prevalence data.

questions.question_text: Which of the following anxiety disorders has the earliest mean age of onset?
questions.explanation:
Separation Anxiety Disorder (Option C): Usually develops in early childhood, typically around 7 years of age.

Social Phobia / Social Anxiety Disorder (Option E): Usually begins in early to mid-adolescence, typically around 13 to 15 years of age.

Panic Disorder (Option B): Generally has an onset in late adolescence to early adulthood, around 20 to 24 years of age.

Situational Phobia (Option D): A subtype of specific phobia (like fear of flying, elevators, or enclosed spaces) that typically has a bimodal onset, often peaking in childhood and then again in the mid-20s.

Generalized Anxiety Disorder (Option A): Often has a more variable onset, but the mean age is generally in early adulthood, around 30 years of age.

questions.question_text: According to the WHO World Mental Health Survey Initiative (Kessler et al., 2010) conducted across 21 countries, which of the following childhood adversities had the lowest reported upper-bound prevalence across countries?
questions.explanation: In the WHO World Mental Health Survey (Kessler et al., 2010), prevalence ranges across 21 countries were: parental death 11.0–14.8%, physical abuse 5.3–10.8%, family violence 4.2–7.8%, and parental mental illness 5.3–6.7%. Parental mental illness had the lowest upper-bound prevalence (6.7%), making it the adversity least prevalent at its highest point across countries. Parental death (A) had the highest prevalence overall, physical abuse (B) reached up to 10.8%, and family violence (D), while having a lower floor (4.2%), reached 7.8% at the upper end. Multiple adversities (E) describes co-occurrence rather than a discrete adversity type with a comparable single-category prevalence.

questions.question_text: In the CATIE study, what was the prevalence of metabolic syndrome at baseline in the group using antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: The CATIE study reported metabolic syndrome prevalence at baseline of 40.9% overall (41% and 43% using different diagnostic criteria), with 51.6% in females and 36% in males.

questions.question_text: In cases of child sexual abuse, girls are victimised compared to boys at approximately which ratio?
questions.explanation: Girls are sexually abused approximately three times more often than boys, giving a ratio of 3:1 (option C). This is a well-established epidemiological finding in child safeguarding literature.

questions.question_text: Which of the following mental disorders shows a notable exception to the rule that anxiety and related disorders are more common in women than men, being equally common in adult men and women?
questions.explanation: OCD is explicitly noted as a \'notable exception\' to the general rule that psychiatric disorders are more common in women: it is more common in boys than girls but equally common in adult men and women (SPMM Paper B, p.335). However, in DSM-5, OCD is classified under \'Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders\' rather than anxiety disorders. Within the anxiety disorders proper, blood-injection-injury phobia (a subtype of specific phobia) is the main exception, with a near-equal sex ratio between men and women (DSM-5-TR p.365; Kaplan & Sadock p.882). All other listed options — panic disorder, generalised anxiety disorder, and specific phobia — are substantially more common in women. If the question is framed around DSM-IV or ICD-10 classification (where OCD was an anxiety disorder), D is correct; under DSM-5/ICD-11, C is the stronger answer within the anxiety disorders category.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman who is pregnant asks about the risk of Down syndrome at her age. What is the approximate risk at age 40?
questions.explanation: Risk of Down syndrome at maternal age 40 is approximately 1:100.

questions.question_text: The female-to-male gender ratio for OCD in community populations is approximately:
questions.explanation: Females predominate in community populations (~1.5:1), this may be because men have more severe psychopathology. The specific ratio of 1.5:1 (female to male) is provided in the OCD epidemiology section. ---

questions.question_text: According to epidemiological data, adversities associated with maladaptive family functioning elevate the risk of adult psychiatric disorders with an odds ratio of:
questions.explanation: The source explicitly states Adversities associated with maladaptive family functioning elevate the risk of adult psychiatric disorders (all major DSM-IV disorders) with an odds ratio of 1.3–2.4. All other ranges are incorrect and not supported by the source.

questions.question_text: In a trial, all participants receive both treatments in sequence with a washout period between. What type of trial design is this?
questions.explanation: In a crossover trial design, each participant serves as their own control and receives all treatments in sequence. Washout periods are necessary between treatments.

questions.question_text: According to the Epidemiological Catchment Area (ECA) study, OCD was found to be the most common psychiatric in which rank (in terms of lifetime prevalence)?
questions.explanation:
In the Epidemiological Catchment Area (ECA) study, OCD was identified as the third most common psychiatric disorder in the general population, with a lifetime prevalence of approximately 2–3%, surpassed only by phobias and alcohol abuse/dependence. 
This ranking is a classic MRCPsych teaching point. Options A (First) and B (Second) are incorrect as MDD and substance/phobic disorders rank higher. Option D (Fourth) and E (Fifth) would place OCD below disorders with lower epidemiological prevalence, which is not supported by ECA or NCS data.

questions.question_text: The ethical guidelines for human research established at the Nuremberg Trials are known as:
questions.explanation: The Nuremberg Code was established following the Nuremberg Trials to establish ethical guidelines for human research.

questions.question_text: Considering epidemiological trends in anxiety disorder presentation, which pattern is documented across successive generations?

options.text: Anxiety disorders are being diagnosed at progressively older ages
Anxiety disorders are being diagnosed at progressively younger ages than previous cohorts
Age of onset has remained stable across generations
Female predominance is decreasing with each generation
Male-to-female ratios are equalizing across all anxiety disorders

correct_answer.text: Anxiety disorders are being diagnosed at progressively younger ages than previous cohorts

questions.explanation: The source explicitly states It is noted that with each generation, anxiety disorders are diagnosed at a younger age than the previous cohort. This documents a secular trend toward earlier diagnosis/onset over time, likely reflecting both earlier recognition and possible aetiological shifts in successive birth cohorts. ---

questions.question_text: The observation that men with OCD show earlier onset and more tics compared to women suggests:

options.text: OCD in males represents a fundamentally different disorder than in females
Males are more accurately diagnosed due to greater symptom severity
A possible neurobiological subtype of OCD with earlier onset and tic-related features may be more prevalent in males
Females have naturally protective factors against all OCD symptom dimensions
Gender differences in OCD are purely psychosocial rather than neurobiological

correct_answer.text: A possible neurobiological subtype of OCD with earlier onset and tic-related features may be more prevalent in males

questions.explanation: Males with OCD showed an earlier onset and a trend toward more tics and poorer outcome than females. This pattern suggests potential biological heterogeneity, with a possible male-predominant OCD subtype characterized by earlier onset, greater tic association, and potentially distinct neurobiological mechanisms involving both serotonergic and dopaminergic systems. ---

questions.question_text: The odds ratio for psychiatric disorder risk in adults who experienced childhood adversities associated with maladaptive family functioning is:

questions.question_text: A drug causes a side effect in 10% of treated patients versus 5% on placebo. What is the number needed to harm (NNH)?
questions.explanation: Absolute Risk Increase (ARI) = 10% − 5% = 5% = 0.05. NNH = 1/ARI = 1/0.05 = 20.

questions.question_text: In a forest plot, a diamond is shown at the bottom. What does the diamond represent?
questions.explanation: The diamond represents the pooled or summary effect estimate from all studies combined in a meta-analysis. Its width represents the confidence interval.

questions.question_text: In a case-control study, cases may remember exposures more accurately than controls. What type of bias is this?
questions.explanation: Recall bias occurs when cases remember past exposures differently (often more thoroughly) than controls because they are actively seeking explanations for their illness.

questions.question_text: A study recruits only patients from tertiary referral centers. What type of bias might this introduce?
questions.explanation: Selection bias or referral bias occurs when recruitment from tertiary centers leads to inclusion of more severe or complex cases, which are not representative of all patients with the condition.

questions.question_text: A community survey examines psychiatric comorbidity in adults with intellectual disability. According to epidemiological surveys, approximately what proportion of people with intellectual disability have a comorbid psychiatric disorder?
questions.explanation: Epidemiological surveys indicate that up to two thirds (~67%) of children and adults with intellectual disability have comorbid psychiatric disorders, a rate several times higher than in community samples without intellectual disability (Kaplan and Sadock\'s Synopsis of Psychiatry 15, p.2393). questions.question_text: The median age of onset for blood-injection-injury phobia is approximately:

questions.explanation: Ecological fallacy occurs when individual-level relationships are inferred from group-level data. Country-level correlations do not prove individual causation.

questions.question_text: Why might the point prevalence estimates for OCD vary between 1-3% depending on methodological factors?

Diagnostic criteria have remained completely static across all studies
